- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.7 → 0.2), model lags; forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment reversal.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For sentiment >0.6 and price >85, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days to avoid peak overshoot.
